title: The week-old service runs out of heap
hook: A Java service throws OutOfMemoryError after a week. Heap dumps show millions of entries in a static HashMap cache.
context: Production service whose cache keys are request-derived strings
solution_brief: The static map retains strong references indefinitely. Use an explicit bounded cache with eviction; a LinkedHashMap access-order LRU is a small single-process option. WeakHashMap is not a size bound and fails if keys stay strongly referenced elsewhere. Confirm retained size and load behavior.

steps.prompt: What is the most direct root cause?

options.text: The static map retains entries without an eviction bound
The garbage collector never scans static fields
Every String key is automatically interned

steps.explanation: A explains growing retained heap. B is false: statics are GC roots. C is not how arbitrary request strings behave.
steps.bottleneck_note: GC cannot reclaim objects still reachable from a static map.
steps.code_snippet:
static final Map<String, Result> CACHE = new HashMap<>();
CACHE.put(requestKey, result);

steps.prompt: A teammate switches to WeakHashMap. What remains risky?

options.text: Eviction depends on key reachability and GC timing, not a predictable capacity
It makes every value weak as well as every key

steps.explanation: A is why it is not a bounded cache. B invents a limit. C misstates WeakHashMap: values remain strong while entries exist.
steps.bottleneck_note: Use weak keys only when key lifetime is the intended ownership rule.
steps.context_note: The team wants a one-line fix.

steps.prompt: Which simple standard-library strategy caps one JVM cache at 10,000 entries?

options.text: A static HashMap plus System.gc() on every insert

steps.explanation: A enforces capacity. B is thread-safe but still unbounded. C cannot collect strongly reachable entries and hurts throughput.
steps.bottleneck_note: Bound entries and estimate bytes per value; count alone may not cap memory tightly.
steps.context_note: The cache does not need to be shared across hosts.

steps.prompt: The cache key is mutated after insertion. Why can lookup fail?

options.text: Its hashCode may change, so it is searched in the wrong bucket
HashMap automatically rehashes the single entry on mutation
equals is never used by HashMap

steps.explanation: A breaks hash-based lookup. B does not happen automatically. C is false: equals resolves candidate keys after hash selection.
steps.bottleneck_note: Use immutable keys whose equals and hashCode agree for their lifetime.
steps.context_note: A new key object contains mutable fields.

steps.prompt: How should the fix be verified under load?

options.text: Track retained heap, cache entry count, hit rate and latency over a sustained test
Run one request and check that it returns 200
Call System.gc() and assume a smaller heap means success

steps.explanation: A checks both memory bound and usefulness. B misses week-long growth. C is not a representative workload or correctness check.
steps.bottleneck_note: A bounded cache that thrashes can trade the leak for latency.
steps.context_note: The eviction policy has been deployed to staging.
